newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ECNZ invites tenders for electricity contracts.
newsitem.headline: ECNZ invites tenders for electricity contracts.

text.p: New Zealand state-owned generator ECNZ on Thursday invited tenders for contracts which it said would allow power companies to secure a fixed price for electricity.
The electricity price contracts, related to ECNZ's firm generation capacity, cover the period of October 1, 1998 to September 30, 2002.
"The tender enables power companies and other electricity buyers to secure a fixed price for electricity," ECNZ said in a statement.
It is the second time electricity price guarantees have been sold in this way in New Zealand.
"Last year's tender was a success, with some 94 percent of the total volume on offer allocated to bidders at prices slightly above reserve," ECNZ (the Electricity Corporation of NZ) said.
This year only one tender round will be held, with a closing date of August 13.
ECNZ said it had been able to agree with customers on a wide range and number of bilateral contracts over the past year.
"For the 12 months from October 1 1997, ECNZ is therefore not offering hedge contracts in this tender as we have already achieved the desired levels of cover."

For the years October 1, 1998 to September 30, 2002, ECNZ will offer the balance between the level of cover already achieved and the level specified in the June 1995 memorandum of understanding between ECNZ and the government.
ECNZ said supply and demand would largely determine the clearing price paid for electricity price guarantees, although minimum reserve prices had been set.

The reserve prices are 4.35 NZ cents per kilowatt-hour for 1998/99 contracts, 4.43 cents for 1999/00, 4.47 for 2000/01, and 4.54 for 2001/02. These were national average base load prices, in nominal terms.
"The prices for the first three years are lower than the reserve prices for the same years in last year's tender and prices reduce in real terms over the period 1998/1999 to 2001/02," ECNZ said.
